raw:
Yewyn Corrford married Kadan Corrley at Kelmere in Chapter 16, and the couple lived in Kelmere from then on. Later paragraphs about her, up to Chapter 37, mention no move. In Chapter 35, Kadan Corrley's planned trip to Salcombe was put off because the roads flooded. Yewyn Haskick, who lives in Salcombe, is a different person.

Answer: Kelmere

Tracing Luena's moves: Staveford (Ch 3), then Dungate (Ch 10), then Wilwick (Ch 13, followed him), then in Ch 31 she left Wilwick and settled in Ostcombe. Later paragraphs (Ch 33: her son moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven) don't say she moved. Ch 31 also notes Rozek went along to Ostcombe.

Answer: Ostcombe

Tracing Fewyn's moves:
- Ch 7: Fewyn followed him to Gulhaven.
- Ch 34: Fewyn moved from Gulhaven to Yarlby.
- Ch 40 ¶6494: "Fewyn followed him to Torton within the month." This is the latest move.

The ch 40 sentence uses just "Fewyn", with no surname, so it is plausibly the same Fewyn Stenworth. Chapter 34's move to Yarlby is the previous known location, and the ch 40 move to Torton is later.

Answer: Torton

Havie Prydenridge moved to Staveford (Ch. 36), then to Dunby (Ch. 39). Isric Thornmere, Havie's spouse, also went to live in Dunby (Ch. 39). The Ch. 40 mentions don't record any further move.

Answer: Dunby

Wenelle moved to Kelmere in Chapter 22 (¶4079), and a child was born there in Chapter 25 and another in Chapter 37 (¶6104), with the family living in Kelmere. The later paragraphs mention no further move for her. The Chapter 10 rumor that she drowned is contradicted by her appearing in later chapters.

Answer: Kelmere

The latest paragraph that places Rinelle is Chapter 35 (¶5834), which says she "went along to live in Torton as well." Earlier she lived in Kelford, then Torton, then Wilholt. Chapter 38 mentions Harine Lindmere moving to Wilwick, but nothing says Rinelle moved there too.

Answer: Torton

Thizek Stenenridge married Movie Prydenridge in Ostcombe (Ch. 28), moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven (Ch. 33), and Movie went along to live there too. In Ch. 38 their daughter Kamira was born, and the family lived in Elmhaven. Nothing later records another move.

Answer: Elmhaven

Lurald Stenworth first lived in Kelford with Luwyn Brackick. After their quarrel he left Kelford for good and took lodgings in Dunstead. In Chapter 25 he married Nerine Prydenridge at Ostcombe, and the couple "lived in Ostcombe from then on." Their son Istho Stenworth was born there. Nothing later records him moving again.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick at Torton in Chapter 34, and the couple lived in Torton from then on. In Chapter 37 their daughter Elvie Brackick was born, and the family lived in Torton. In Chapter 38 Pelde is still in Torton, and the later paragraphs about people moving away do not mention her.

Answer: Torton

Gadrek Prydenridge married in Chapter 29 and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. No later paragraph in the record says he moved. Chapter 31 has Rozek Stenenridge going to live in Ostcombe, which fits Gadrek still being there, and the later Chapter 36 paragraphs that mention him don't show a move either.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenson is the third child of Matho Stenson and Ismira Stenson. In Chapter 8 she married Davus Stenworth at Torton, and the couple lived in Torton from then on. In Chapter 15 their daughter Dalis was born and the family lived in Torton. No later paragraph about her records a move, so Torton is the latest known residence.

Answer: Torton

Nylia died in Chapter 5 (¶1731). Jotho lived in Ostcombe from the start (Chapter 1). He married in Chapter 16 and lived in Ostcombe from then on, and he did not leave Ostcombe for Quenford until Chapter 39. So at Nylia's death in Chapter 5, he was in Ostcombe.

Answer: Ostcombe

Malis Prydenridge died in Chapter 7 (¶2097). Peten's moves: lived in Dunstead (Ch. 1), still in Dunstead in Ch. 11 and Ch. 13, then moved to Staveford in Ch. 14 (¶2941). Chapter 7 comes before the move to Staveford, so he was still in Dunstead.

Answer: Dunstead

Islan died in Chapter 29 (¶4979) at Dungate. Gadrek's residence at that time: in Chapter 29 ¶4995, he married the eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in the chapel at Ostcombe, and the couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Ordering within Chapter 29: Islan's death is ¶4979, and the marriage is ¶4995, which comes later. Before that, Gadrek lived in Ostcombe (family home, no move recorded). Either way, he lived in Ostcombe.

Answer: Ostcombe

Ulrald Corrford died in Chapter 21 (buried at Staveford).

Pelde Stenson married Davus Stenworth in Chapter 8 and lived in Torton from then on. In Chapter 15 their daughter Dalis was born, and the family lived in Torton. In Chapter 24, Matho Stenson went to live in Elmhaven, but nothing says Pelde moved. Chapter 24 shows Pelde Stenson arguing with the carter, which gives no location. Chapter 32 is later than Ulrald's death, and it places Pelde Stenson in Torton.

The latest information before Chapter 21 puts Pelde Stenson in Torton.

Answer: Torton

Pewyn died in Chapter 19 (¶3597).

Taric's moves up to that point:
- Chapter 16: he left Kelmere and took lodgings in Staveford.
- Chapter 23: he left Staveford for Dungate. This is after Pewyn's death.

Chapter 19 falls after Chapter 16 and before Chapter 23, so Taric was in Staveford when Pewyn died.

Answer: Staveford

Nelan died in Chapter 16 (¶3169). Rorald's moves: lived in Kelmere (Ch. 1), and at Ch. 16 ¶3245 he is in the river crossing at Kelmere, which comes after the death paragraph ¶3169 and is the latest location before the move to Salcombe in Ch. 19. So at the time of Nelan's death, he was in Kelmere.

Answer: Kelmere

Orrald the Younger died in Chapter 8 (¶2174). At that time, Havie Prydenridge was in Ostcombe (¶2209, Chapter 8, "In Ostcombe. Havie read the almanac..."). She only moved to Staveford in Chapter 36, much later.

Answer: Ostcombe

Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick at Torton in Chapter 34, and the couple lived in Torton from then on. Chapter 37 has their daughter Elvie Brackick born into a family living in Torton. Chapter 39 records Marald Corrford's death, and nothing between Chapter 34 and that point moves Pelde away from Torton.

Answer: Torton

Ismira Stenson died in Chapter 37 (¶6015). Kassa Stenson's moves, in order:

- Chapter 1: lived in Kelmere, married to Taric Corrley.
- Chapter 16: went to live in Staveford.
- Chapter 23: went to live in Dungate.
- Chapter 34: went to live in Kelmere.

Her latest move before Ismira's death was the Chapter 34 move to Kelmere. Ismira herself was buried at Kelmere.

Answer: Kelmere

Gazek Stenson died in Chapter 5 (¶1757). Thizek Stenenridge lived in the harbor town of Dunstead (Chapter 1), and he did not marry and move to Ostcombe until Chapter 28. Nothing earlier than Chapter 5 shows him moving, and the Chapter 2 paragraphs also place him in Dunstead.

Answer: Dunstead

Ludrek Prydenridge died in Chapter 11 (¶2530).

Havus Stenworth's moves:
- Chapter 1: lived in Torton.
- Chapter 7 (¶1942): rode out of Torton and was living in Gulhaven by the next market day.
- Chapter 34 (¶5616): went to live in Yarlby, which is after Chapter 11.
- Chapter 40 (¶6487): rode out of Yarlby and went to Torton.

Between Chapter 7 and Chapter 34, no other move is recorded. At the time of Ludrek's death in Chapter 11, Havus was therefore still in Gulhaven.

Answer: Gulhaven

Harine Lindmere first married Orrald Stenson (Chapter 1) and lived in Torton. In Chapter 8, "Orrald the Younger died of a wound that festered at Torton." This may be a different Orrald, though Orrald Stenson was the son of Matho Stenson. Orrald is also mentioned in Chapter 7 as alive, before Chapter 8. If Orrald Stenson died there, Harine would be widowed.

In Chapter 33, "the eldest daughter of Rorald Lindmere took Ilrald Prydenridge in marriage at Torton. The couple lived in Torton from then on." The eldest daughter is Harine. In Chapter 38, Ilrald Prydenridge left Torton and settled in Wilwick, and "Harine went along to live in Wilwick as well." So she is still married to Ilrald Prydenridge, with no record of his death.

Answer: Ilrald Prydenridge

Zalis Corrley's first husband, Gadan Corrley, died in Chapter 18. In Chapter 26, Ferald and Zalis Corrley were wed at Dunstead. Nothing later records a death or a separation, so Ferald is the spouse at the end. The record gives only the first name, Ferald, with no surname.

Answer: Ferald

Pelde Stenworth's first husband, Gazek Stenson, died in Chapter 5. In Chapter 34 she married Sebin Brackick at Torton. Sebin is still alive in Chapter 38, where he is shown falling asleep in the chair, and nothing later records his death or a further marriage for her.

Answer: Sebin Brackick

Pelde Stenson is the daughter of Matho Stenson, and she is a different person from Pelde Stenworth, the daughter of Havus Stenworth.

- Gazek Stenson married Pelde Stenworth, then died in Chapter 5.
- In Chapter 8, Davus Stenworth and Pelde Stenson were wed at Torton.
- In Chapter 15, a daughter, Dalis Stenworth, was born to Pelde Stenson and Davus Stenworth.
- In Chapter 34, Pelde Stenworth married Sebin Brackick. That is the other Pelde and does not affect Pelde Stenson's marriage.
- Davus Stenworth is still mentioned as active in Chapters 37 and 38, and no death or other change to the marriage appears.

Answer: Davus Stenworth

Peten Haskick is Lura's husband (Chapter 1). He moved from Dunstead to Staveford, Lura followed him there, and then they both went to Quenford. In Chapter 39 Peten rode out of Quenford to Gulhaven, and Lura went along to live in Gulhaven as well. No death or separation is recorded for either, so the marriage still stands.

Answer: Peten Haskick

Yewyn Corrford married Kadan Corrley at Kelmere in Chapter 16. Kadan Corrley appears alive in later chapters (Chapter 35 and Chapter 37), and nothing in the record shows a death or other end to the marriage.

Answer: Kadan Corrley

Havus Stenworth's wife was Fewyn Stenworth from the start. Later events: Fewyn followed him to Gulhaven (ch. 7), Havus moved to Yarlby (ch. 34), and in ch. 40 he rode from Yarlby to Torton, with "Fewyn followed him to Torton within the month." No death or divorce is recorded for either.

Answer: Fewyn Stenworth

Kadan Corrley married Yewyn Corrford in Chapter 16, and the two lived in Kelmere. Chapter 19 still shows them together, with Yewyn Corrford answering Kadan. Nothing later records Yewyn's death or a separation. The Chapter 26 marriage of Zalis Corrley and Ferald concerns Kadan's mother, not Kadan.

Answer: Yewyn Corrford

Movie married the only son of Luena Stenenridge in Chapter 28. Luena's children are Thizek and Pewyn, so the only son is Thizek Stenenridge. Chapter 38 confirms it: Movie and Thizek had a daughter, Kamira, and the family lived in Elmhaven. Nothing in the record says Thizek died.

Answer: Thizek Stenenridge

Isric Thornmere married Havie (Prydenridge) in Chapter 28 at Ostcombe. No later paragraph mentions a death or a separation, and no other marriage for Isric appears. Chapters 36 and 39 say Isric followed "her" to Staveford and went along to live in Dunby, but those are moves, not changes of marital status. Chapter 40 still has Havie Prydenridge and Isric together.

Answer: Havie Prydenridge

Ferald Stenworth married Zalis Corrley at Dunstead in Chapter 26, and they lived there from then on. Nothing later in the record mentions Zalis's death or a new marriage for Ferald. A later paragraph (Chapter 31) has Zavus Prydenridge speaking to Zalis, so she was still alive then.

Answer: Zalis Corrley

Chapter 29 (¶4995) says Gadrek Prydenridge married the eldest daughter of Lura Haskick, who is Yera Haskick, in the chapel at Ostcombe. No later paragraph mentions her being widowed or remarried, and Gadrek appears alive in Chapter 39. The Chapter 27 claim that Islan Thornmere secretly married her is only a whisper from Kassa Brackick, so it does not count as fact.

Answer: Gadrek Prydenridge

Movus Brackick married Dalis Stenworth in the chapel at Yarlby in Chapter 39. In Chapter 40 they had a son, Iszek Brackick, and the family lived in Yarlby. Nothing in the record says Dalis Stenworth died or that the marriage ended.

Answer: Dalis Stenworth

Luena Stenenridge is married to Rozek Stenenridge. They appear together through the record, with the last mentions in Chapter 37 ("Rozek Stenenridge and Luena talked of nothing much"), and no death or separation is recorded for him. Chapter 39 also has Rozek in a conversation, so he is still alive late in the record.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

Bremira Corrford married Zavus Prydenridge in Chapter 25. Zavus is still named alive in Chapter 31 (¶5195). Nothing in the record says he died or that they separated. The only death mentioned is Rovus Prydenridge, who is Zavus's father, and Bremira's account of it in ¶5186 is only a report of a drowning. It has no bearing on Zavus.

Answer: Zavus Prydenridge

Chapter 18 states that Yedan Corrford died of a kick from a cart horse at Dunstead. Nothing later in the record reverses this.

Answer: no

Orrald Stenson ("Orrald the Younger") is recorded in Chapter 8 (¶2174) as having died of a wound that festered at Torton. Nothing later in the record says he is alive again.

Answer: no

Chapter 5 ¶1757 states that Gazek Stenson died of a wound that festered at Torton. Nothing later in the record says otherwise, so he is not alive at the end.

Answer: no

Chapter 29 ¶4979 states that Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in his sleep at Dungate. The only other claim is Rorald's report in Chapter 12 that Islan drowned, which is a rumor, and Islan appears alive afterward anyway. Chapter 33 has Vesmira marrying Rimor Corrford, which is consistent with Islan having died earlier. Nothing later shows Islan alive.

Answer: no

Gadan Corrley is the husband of Zalis Corrley (Chapter 1, ¶111). Chapter 18, ¶3478 says her husband died of a long wasting sickness at Kelmere. Nothing later contradicts this; the Chapter 22 paragraph only mentions his youngest son.

Answer: No

Chapter 37 ¶6015 says a festering wound took Ismira Stenson that summer and she was buried at Kelmere. The earlier plague rumor in Chapter 8 was false, but this death is stated as fact. After it, the only mention is that the bone compass she had owned went to Matho Stenson, which confirms she was gone.

Answer: no

In Chapter 16 (¶3169), the record says the coughing sickness took Nelan that spring and that he was buried at Kelford. Later paragraphs mention him only as a parent, for example "the youngest son of Nelan Brackick", and none of them say he returned or was alive. So he is not alive at the end of the record.

Answer: no

In Chapter 21, Ulrald Corrford was buried in the churchyard at Staveford, dead of old age. His belongings, the silver flute and the amber map, went to Kassa Brackick. Nothing later in the record says he is alive again.

Answer: no

Chapter 7 records that Malis Prydenridge was buried in the churchyard at Ostcombe, dead of a long wasting sickness. Nothing later in the record says otherwise. The Chapter 37 letter is from her youngest son, not from her.

Answer: no

The latest relevant paragraph is Chapter 39 ¶6312, which says they laid Marald Corrford in the churchyard at Ravenmere, dead of a fall from the mill loft. No later paragraph says he is alive.

Answer: no

Chapter 5 states that a long wasting sickness took Nylia Corrford that summer and that she was buried at Dunstead. Nothing later in the record contradicts this, so she is not alive at the end.

Answer: no

In Chapter 22, ¶4134, the record says Volia Brackick was laid in the churchyard at Kelford, dead of drowning in the flood. Later paragraphs that mention a Volia Brackick (Chapter 14 and 16) come earlier than this. Nothing after Chapter 22 says she is alive again.

Answer: no

The only claim of death is a rumor in Chapter 10, where Ismira Stenson says Wenelle drowned crossing the estuary, though no body was ever seen. That is gossip, not fact. Wenelle appears in many later paragraphs. She gives birth to Ilrald in Chapter 19, moves to Kelmere in Chapter 22, bears Febin in Chapter 25, and bears Madan in Chapter 37. In Chapter 37 she also speaks and acts in several paragraphs. No later paragraph reports her death.

Answer: yes

The record contains no event in which Matho Stenson dies. The two plague rumors (Chapters 18 and 24) are unconfirmed, so they are not facts. He is last mentioned in Chapter 39, where he sends a parcel containing the bone compass to Luvie Prydenridge, so he is still alive at that point.

Answer: yes

Pelde Stenworth's last mentions are in Chapter 38, where she walks the long way round, shrugs when asked about rain, and talks with Davus. The only claim of her death is the Chapter 21 plague rumor, which is not a fact. She also married Sebin Brackick in Chapter 34 and had a daughter in Chapter 37. Nothing says she died.

Answer: yes

Matho Stenson is last mentioned in Chapter 39, where he sends a parcel to Luvie Prydenridge, so he is still acting then. The two plague-death reports about him (Chapters 18 and 24) are rumors started by Kassa Brackick and Pelde Stenson, and rumors are not facts. Nothing in the record states that he died.

Answer: yes

The only death claim is the Chapter 30 rumor that Rorald Lindmere was dead of plague, started by Movie Prydenridge from a peddler. Rumors are not facts. He appears alive and active in Chapter 40, the last chapter, where he talks with Pelia, sorts letters and buys a ribbon in Yarlby.

Answer: yes

The only claim of death is Bremira's statement in Chapter 31 that Rovus drowned crossing the estuary. It is a rumor, and no body was ever seen. After that, Rovus appears alive and active: in Chapter 32 he complains of an aching back and argues with the carter, in Chapter 35 he speaks at the river crossing in Kelmere, and in Chapter 37 he talks with Wenelle and a son, Madan, is born to them. No later paragraph reports his death.

Answer: yes

The record's last mention of Ilrald Prydenridge is in Chapter 38, which says he left Torton and settled in Wilwick. Nothing in the record reports his death, and the Chapter 31 story about drowning concerns Rovus Prydenridge, who is a different person. So the latest information shows him alive.

Answer: yes

No paragraph records the death of Yewyn Corrford. She appears alive in the latest entries, in Chapter 37. The only Corrford death near the end is her brother Marald Corrford in Chapter 39.

Answer: yes

No death of Kassa Stenson appears in the record. The latest mentions in Chapter 37 show her sorting old letters, and nothing afterward reports her dying. The only death noted among the Stensons is Gazek Stenson's (Chapter 5). The rumors about other Stensons being dead of plague are not facts.

Answer: yes

The latest paragraph about Bremira Corrford is in Chapter 39, where a parcel from Lura Haskick reached her and the silver chalice became hers to keep. That shows her alive then. No record of her death appears anywhere in the material.

Answer: yes

Istho Stenworth appears from Chapter 25 (birth) through Chapter 39 (speaking to Yera). No death is recorded anywhere in the material, so the latest information shows Istho still alive.

Answer: yes

Kassa Brackick appears in paragraphs through Chapter 40, the last chapter, still active (arguing with the carter, telling Jotho Thornmere about the ledger). No death is recorded for her.

Answer: yes

The latest paragraph about Taric Corrley (Chapter 37, ¶6116) has him reading the almanac aloud, so he is alive. The record contains no mention of his death. Kassa Stenson is described as his wife, and nothing says he died.

Answer: yes

The silver flute belonged to Ulrald Corrford, then went to Kassa Brackick (Chapter 21). No later mention transfers it. The chalice moves around, but that's a separate object. The vault law in Chapter 1 doesn't change the holder.

Answer: Kassa Brackick

The jade mirror starts with Rozek Stenenridge. It then passes between him and Luena Stenenridge several times. The last transfer is in Chapter 36, where Rozek gives it to Luvie Prydenridge and takes nothing for it. No later passage moves it again.

Answer: Luvie Prydenridge

Tracing the oak lantern: Luena Stenenridge kept it, then gave it to Rozek Stenenridge (Ch. 12). Rozek sent it to Rovus Prydenridge (Ch. 18). Wenelle Lindmere won it from Rovus at cards and kept it (Ch. 19). No later change is recorded.

Answer: Wenelle Lindmere

The copper chalice's last recorded change of hands is in Chapter 35, where Isric Thornmere won it from Gadrek Prydenridge at cards, fairly, and kept it. Earlier, Luena Stenenridge sent it to Yera Stenworth (Chapter 29), and Gadrek then won it from Yera (Chapter 31).

Answer: Isric Thornmere

Tracing the oak comb: Isric Thornmere possessed it (Ch.1), then Isric sent it by carrier to Kassa Brackick, who received it safely (Ch.22). No later transfer is mentioned.

Answer: Kassa Brackick

The pewter dagger passed through these hands:

- It began with Yewyn Haskick (Ch. 1).
- Yewyn gave it to the youngest son of Volia Brackick (Ch. 19).
- The youngest son of Nelan Brackick sent it to Jotho Thornmere, who was to keep it (Ch. 20). I took this to be the same youngest son, though the record names his parent differently.
- Yera Stenworth won it from Quiet Jotho at cards, fairly, and kept it (Ch. 40). I took Quiet Jotho to be Jotho Thornmere.

Gadrek's later win from Yera Stenworth was a copper chalice, not the dagger, so nothing later in the record moves the dagger on.

Answer: Yera Stenworth

The brass map belonged to Ismira Stenson (¶1087), who later gave it to Matho Stenson (¶2977). No later passage moves it again.

Answer: Matho Stenson

The latest paragraph about the amber map (Chapter 33, ¶5459) says Volan Stenworth pressed it into the hands of Rimor Corrford. Nothing later records it changing hands.

Answer: Rimor Corrford

Tracing the silver chalice: it started with Kassa Brackick (Ch. 1), who pressed it into the hands of Quiet Peten (Ch. 5). Peten Haskick then pressed it into the hands of Lura Haskick (Ch. 19). In Ch. 39, a parcel from Lura Haskick reached Bremira Corrford, and the silver chalice inside was now hers to keep. That is the latest relevant information.

Answer: Bremira Corrford

The ivory lantern belonged to Ismira Stenson (¶1137). In Chapter 32 (¶5393), Ismira Stenson pressed it into the hands of Rimor Corrford and took nothing for it. No later paragraph shows it changing hands again.

Answer: Rimor Corrford

The latest paragraph about the bone compass (Chapter 39, ¶6429) says a parcel from Matho Stenson reached Luvie Prydenridge, and inside was the bone compass, now hers to keep. No later paragraph mentions it moving again.

Answer: Luvie Prydenridge

The ivory chalice belonged to Ludrek Prydenridge (¶1171). By custom it passes only when its holder dies, going to the holder's eldest living child (¶1367). Nothing in the material says Ludrek died or that the chalice changed hands. The later chalice transfers all involve the copper and silver chalices, not the ivory one.

Answer: Ludrek Prydenridge

The silver flute belonged to Ulrald Corrford (Ch. 1), then went to Kassa Brackick (Ch. 21). No later transfer is recorded, so Kassa Brackick is the current holder and Ulrald Corrford held it immediately before.

Answer: Ulrald Corrford

The jade mirror's latest transfer is in Chapter 36, where Rozek Stenenridge gave it to Luvie Prydenridge, so Luvie is the current holder. Just before that, in Chapter 23, Luena Stenenridge had given it to Rozek, so Rozek held it immediately before Luvie.

Answer: Rozek Stenenridge

The oak lantern's chain of holders: Luena Stenenridge kept it, then gave it to Rozek Stenenridge (Ch. 12). Rozek sent it to Rovus Prydenridge (Ch. 18). Wenelle Lindmere won it from Rovus at cards (Ch. 19) and kept it, so she is the current holder.

The holder immediately before Wenelle Lindmere was Rovus Prydenridge.

Answer: Rovus Prydenridge

The copper chalice passed through these holders in order:

- Luena Stenenridge sent it to Yera Stenworth (Ch. 29).
- Gadrek won it from Yera Stenworth at cards (Ch. 31).
- Isric Thornmere won it from Gadrek Prydenridge at cards (Ch. 35). This is the latest event, so Isric Thornmere is the current holder.

The holder immediately before Isric Thornmere was Gadrek. The Ch. 35 passage calls him Gadrek Prydenridge, and I take the "Gadrek" of Ch. 31 to be the same person.

Answer: Gadrek Prydenridge

The oak comb: Isric Thornmere possessed it (Ch.1), then Isric sent it by carrier to Kassa Brackick, who received it safely (Ch.22). So the current holder is Kassa Brackick, and the one immediately before was Isric Thornmere.

Answer: Isric Thornmere

The pewter dagger started with Yewyn Haskick, who gave it to the youngest son of a Brackick. It then reached Jotho Thornmere by parcel. In Chapter 40, Yera Stenworth won it at cards from "Quiet Jotho", whom I take to be Jotho Thornmere, and kept it. That makes Yera Stenworth the current holder, and the holder immediately before was Jotho Thornmere.

Answer: Jotho Thornmere

Brass map history: it belonged to Ismira Stenson (Ch. 1), and Ismira gave it to Matho Stenson (Ch. 14). That is the latest information, so Matho Stenson is the current holder and Ismira Stenson held it immediately before.

Answer: Ismira Stenson

Chain of holders: Tatho Brackick → Marald Corrford → Ulrald Corrford → Kassa Brackick → Volan Stenworth → Rimor Corrford (current holder).

The holder immediately before Rimor Corrford was Volan Stenworth.

Answer: Volan Stenworth

Silver chalice chain: Kassa Brackick owned it (Ch 1), then pressed it into the hands of Quiet Peten (Ch 5). Then Peten Haskick pressed it into the hands of Lura Haskick (Ch 19). Then a parcel from Lura Haskick reached Bremira Corrford (Ch 39), who now keeps it.

The current holder is Bremira Corrford, and the one immediately before was Lura Haskick.

Answer: Lura Haskick

The ivory lantern: first belonged to Ismira Stenson (Ch 1), and in Chapter 32 Ismira Stenson gave it to Rimor Corrford. So the current holder is Rimor Corrford, and the one immediately before was Ismira Stenson.

Answer: Ismira Stenson

The latest paragraph (Chapter 39, ¶6429) says a parcel from Matho Stenson reached Luvie Prydenridge, with the bone compass inside, now hers to keep. So Luvie Prydenridge is the current holder, and the one before her was Matho Stenson.

Answer: Matho Stenson

Movie Prydenridge's father is Rovus Prydenridge (Chapter 6). Rovus is the son of Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge (Chapter 1). So the paternal grandfather is Ludrek Prydenridge.

Answer: Ludrek Prydenridge

Rimor Corrford's mother is Kassa Brackick, who was born into the Brackick household in Kelford, the daughter of Nelan Brackick and Volia Brackick. Volia Brackick is therefore Rimor's maternal grandmother.

Answer: Volia Brackick

Madan's father is Rovus Prydenridge, whose parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. His paternal grandmother is therefore Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Nerine's father is Rovus Prydenridge. Rovus is the son of Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge, so his mother Malis Prydenridge is Nerine's paternal grandmother.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Iszek Brackick's mother is Dalis Stenworth. The record names her parents nowhere, so her mother can't be identified.

The Stenworth links I can see are Lurald Stenworth (married to Luwyn Brackick), Volan Stenworth and Pelde Stenworth. Nothing connects any of them to Dalis as her mother.

Iszek's father is Movus Brackick, son of Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick. That makes Rinelle Corrley his paternal grandmother, not his maternal one.

Answer: unknown

Istho Stenworth's parents are Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth. The father, Lurald Stenworth, is the son of Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth (Chapter 1 household). So the paternal grandmother is Fewyn Stenworth.

Answer: Fewyn Stenworth

Febin's father is Rovus Prydenridge, whose parents are Ludrek Prydenridge and Malis Prydenridge. His paternal grandmother is therefore Malis Prydenridge.

Answer: Malis Prydenridge

Ferald Stenworth's father is Lurald Stenworth (born to Luwyn Brackick and Lurald Stenworth). Lurald Stenworth's parents are Havus Stenworth and Fewyn Stenworth, the Torton household where Lurald is listed as a son. So the paternal grandfather is Havus Stenworth.

Answer: Havus Stenworth

Elra Corrford's parents are Fenelle Lindmere and Marald Corrford. Her maternal grandfather is therefore the father of Fenelle Lindmere. Fenelle is one of the three daughters of Rorald Lindmere and Pelia Lindmere.

Answer: Rorald Lindmere

Bremira Corrford is the daughter of Kassa Brackick and Ulrald Corrford. Ulrald Corrford is the eldest son of Yedan Corrford and Nylia Corrford. Her paternal grandfather is therefore Yedan Corrford (who later died from a kick by a cart horse).

Answer: Yedan Corrford
